selected_evidence.summary: Account exists as UID/GID 1000 with the requested login environment and persisted after restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Login sessions are limited to 8,192 open files and 256 processes
selected_evidence.summary: Persistent PAM configuration was installed; fresh appworker login sessions reported soft/hard nofile=8192 and nproc=256 before and after restart.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28; reboot was acknowledged; recovered node used changed boot ID 9f792d71-9bfd-441f-943d-6ab7f847b1b3, was running with zero failed units, and retained the account and effective limits.

commands.command:
set -eu
printf 'node=%s ip=%s\n' "$NODE_NAME" "$NODE_IP"
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf 'account='; if getent passwd appworker >/dev/null; then getent passwd appworker; else echo absent; fi
printf '%s\n' 'limits_matches:'
grep -RnsE '^[[:space:]]*appworker[[:space:]]+(soft|hard|-)[[:space:]]+(nofile|nproc)[[:space:]]+' /etc/security/limits.conf /etc/security/limits.d 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s\n' 'pam_limits:'
grep -RnsE '^[[:space:]]*session[[:space:]]+required[[:space:]]+pam_limits\.so' /etc/pam.d 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s\n' 'services:'
systemctl is-system-running || true
systemctl --failed --no-legend || true
commands.stdout:
node=node1 ip=10.100.201.10
boot_id=646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28
account=absent
limits_matches:
pam_limits:
/etc/pam.d/runuser:4:session		required	pam_limits.so
/etc/pam.d/system-auth:18:session     required                                     pam_limits.so
/etc/pam.d/password-auth:[REDACTED]]]]     required                                     pam_limits.so
services:
running

commands.command:
set -eu
if ! getent passwd appworker >/dev/null; then useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash appworker; fi
getent passwd appworker
id appworker

set -eu
umask 022
printf '%s\n' '# Managed resource limits for appworker login sessions' 'appworker - nofile 8192' 'appworker - nproc 256' > /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf
chown root:root /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf
chmod 0644 /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf
stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf
sed -n '1,20p' /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf
commands.stdout:
root:root 644 /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf
# Managed resource limits for appworker login sessions
appworker - nofile 8192
appworker - nproc 256

commands.command:
set -eu
runuser -l appworker -c 'printf "user=%s
" "$(id -un)"; printf "nofile_soft=%s
" "$(ulimit -Sn)"; printf "nofile_hard=%s
" "$(ulimit -Hn)"; printf "nproc_soft=%s
" "$(ulimit -Su)"; printf "nproc_hard=%s
" "$(ulimit -Hu)"; test "$(ulimit -Sn)" = 8192; test "$(ulimit -Hn)" = 8192; test "$(ulimit -Su)" = 256; test "$(ulimit -Hu)" = 256'
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf 'system_state='; systemctl is-system-running
printf 'failed_units='; systemctl --failed --no-legend | wc -l
commands.stdout:
user=appworker
nofile_soft=8192
nofile_hard=8192
nproc_soft=256
nproc_hard=256
boot_id=646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28
system_state=running
failed_units=0
